name: Bring an Existing OpenAI Agents SDK App to Conductor with Minimal Changes
query: We already have an OpenAI Agents SDK app in Python: an `Agent` with `instructions`, three `@function_tool` functions, and we run it with `Runner.run_sync(agent, prompt)`. I want it running on Conductor with the fewest possible changes. What exactly do I change?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Consult references/agents.md (decision table → path 3 'bring your framework'; framework execution model — OpenAI Agents is compiled into a Conductor graph) and references/agent-sdks.md (OpenAI Agents SDK row for Python: drop-in `Runner` or pass the `agents.Agent` to `AgentRuntime`).

Step 2: Preflight — `conductor agent list`; `GET /api/providers/status` shows `openai` configured. Explain that because the agent is compiled, the LLM turns run server-side as `LLM_CHAT_COMPLETE`, so `OPENAI_API_KEY` must be on the Conductor server.
Step 3: WebFetch the Python SDK `docs/agents/` framework page; install `pip install 'conductor-python[openai-agents]'`.

Step 4: Minimal-change path: replace `from agents import Runner, function_tool` with `from conductor.ai import Runner, function_tool`; keep `Agent`, `instructions`, the three tools and `Runner.run_sync(agent, prompt)` untouched. Mention `Runner.run` / `Runner.run_streamed` are also available.

Step 5: Alternative path: keep the `agents` imports and pass the OpenAI `Agent` object directly — `AgentRuntime().run(openai_agent, prompt)` / `deploy(openai_agent)` / `serve(openai_agent)`. Note the normalizer carries over handoffs, guardrails and `output_type` (ask whether the app uses them).

Step 6: State that `@function_tool` functions become worker tools: for production `runtime.deploy(...)` registers and a long-lived `runtime.serve(...)` process executes them; without `serve()` tool calls hang.

Step 7: Model ends up as `openai/<model>`; if the code sets a model, keep it explicit. Any workflow invocation uses `AGENT` with `agentType: "conductor"` + `name` — never `agentType: "openai"`. Never recommend `conductor deploy`.
success_criteria: Offers the drop-in `from conductor.ai import Runner` (with or without also swapping `function_tool`) as the minimal-change path, keeping `Runner.run_sync(agent, prompt)` and the existing `Agent`/tools code
Also mentions the alternative of passing the OpenAI Agents SDK `Agent` object directly to `AgentRuntime().run/deploy/serve`
Install is `pip install 'conductor-python[openai-agents]'` (or `[agents]`) — no invented package

Explains that LLM turns run server-side (the agent is compiled into a Conductor graph) so `OPENAI_API_KEY` must be configured on the Conductor server (checked via `GET /api/providers/status`), not only in the app's environment
States that `@function_tool` functions are worker tools that need a `runtime.serve(...)` process in production, and that `deploy()` alone does not run them
Does not rewrite the app into a native Conductor `Agent`/`@tool` form or a hand-wired DO_WHILE loop — the user's Agent, instructions and tools are kept
Any workflow-side invocation uses `type: "AGENT"`, `agentType: "conductor"`, `name: "<deployed name>"` — `agentType: "openai"` never appears
WebFetches the Python SDK `docs/agents/` (or README) before pinning install/version, and never recommends `conductor deploy`
Mentions that handoffs / guardrails / `output_type` are carried over by the bridge, or asks whether the app uses them — does not claim they must be dropped
